cmd_hostd_ask_restart: Question of `atlas hostd --reconcile` in a terminal, before [y/N]; only asked when terminals are running, so {count} is at least 1.
cmd_hostd_check_fix: Heading of the commands that bring the terminal host up to date, in `atlas hostd --check`.

cmd_hostd_check_fix_asks.description: Comment after the `atlas hostd --reconcile` command in the fix list, when the host cannot hand over and no terminal runs.
cmd_hostd_check_fix_asks.distinct: comment next to a shell command, lowercase

cmd_hostd_check_fix_asks_ends.description: Comment after the `atlas hostd --reconcile` command in the fix list, when the host cannot hand over and terminals run (listed above).
cmd_hostd_check_fix_asks_ends.distinct: comment next to a shell command, lowercase

cmd_hostd_check_fix_live.description: Comment after the `atlas hostd --reconcile` command in the fix list, when the host can hand its terminals over live.
cmd_hostd_check_fix_live.distinct: comment next to a shell command, lowercase

cmd_hostd_check_fix_restart.description: Comment after the `atlas hostd --restart` command in the fix list.
cmd_hostd_check_fix_restart.distinct: comment next to a shell command, lowercase

cmd_hostd_check_not_running: Output of `atlas hostd --check` (exit code 1) when no terminal host answers in the directory {dir}.
cmd_hostd_check_older: First line of `atlas hostd --check` when the host is older than this Atlas but nothing the app needs is missing. {uptime} is a compact duration such as 40h or 4d 4h.
cmd_hostd_check_older_features: First line of `atlas hostd --check` when the host lacks a capability the app needs. {features} is the list of what is off (cmd_hostd_features_list).
cmd_hostd_check_running_terminals: Heading of the list of running terminals (working directory and command per line) in `atlas hostd --check`.
cmd_hostd_crew_paused: Output of `atlas hostd --crew-pause`: the crew stops starting new tasks.
cmd_hostd_crew_resumed: Output of `atlas hostd --crew-resume`: the crew starts new tasks again.

cmd_hostd_ctx_handoff.description: Context of the `upgrade` request to hostd (the hand-over of the running terminals to this binary); shown in the cause chain of the failed live upgrade.
cmd_hostd_ctx_handoff.distinct: name of a step in an error chain, not a button

cmd_hostd_current: Output of `atlas hostd --check` and `--reconcile` when the running terminal host matches this Atlas version.
cmd_hostd_disconnected: Error of `atlas term wait` when the connection to hostd drops while waiting for a terminal. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.
cmd_hostd_exported: Summary line of `atlas hostd --crew-export` on stderr (stdout carries the archive); {count} is the number of crewmates in the archive.
cmd_hostd_feature_agents: What is off while the terminal host is old: the state of coding agents (working, waiting) in terminal tabs. Capability `agents` of hostd.
cmd_hostd_feature_lsp: What is off while the terminal host is old: editor features from language servers (hover, diagnostics, go to definition). Capability `lsp` of hostd.
cmd_hostd_feature_pty_attach_raw: What is off while the terminal host is old: the raw byte stream that renders terminals quickly. Capability `pty_attach_raw` of hostd.
cmd_hostd_features_list: The features a stale terminal host cannot offer, joined as a list: one, two or three names (cmd_hostd_feature_*) in {first}, {second}, {third}; {count} says how many.
cmd_hostd_imported: One line per crewmate of `atlas hostd --crew-import`: its name and the id it has on this server.
cmd_hostd_imported_renamed: Line of `atlas hostd --crew-import` for a crewmate whose id changed on import (a clash, or --rename): the new id and the id it had in the archive.
cmd_hostd_kept: Last line of `atlas hostd --reconcile` when the person declined (or could not be asked) to end the running terminals. The two commands stay as typed.
cmd_hostd_login_no_terminal: Context of `atlas hostd --crew-login`: hostd accepted the engine sign-in request but returned no terminal to attach. Shown after `caused by:`.
cmd_hostd_not_running: Output of `atlas hostd --reconcile`, `--restart` and `atlas update` when no terminal host runs: the app starts a current one on demand.
cmd_hostd_not_running_desktop: Error of `atlas term` when no hostd answers and the desktop app is closed. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.
cmd_hostd_not_running_in: Error of `atlas hostd` (--status, --stop, --upgrade, --mobile-pair, --crew-pause, --crew-login): no daemon answers in the hostd directory {dir}. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.
cmd_hostd_pair_no_address: Error of `atlas hostd --mobile-pair` when the pairing invite carries neither a relay nor a direct address. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.
cmd_hostd_reconcile_upgraded: Output of `atlas hostd --reconcile` and `atlas update` after a live hand-over; {count} is how many running terminals the new host kept.
cmd_hostd_restarted_ended: Output of `atlas hostd --restart`, `--reconcile` and `atlas update` after the terminal host was replaced; {count} is how many running terminals ended with the old one.
cmd_hostd_restarted_idle: Output of `atlas hostd --reconcile` and `atlas update` when the stale host had no running terminal and was replaced without asking.
cmd_hostd_stop_timeout: Error of a restart: the old terminal host still answered ten seconds after the shutdown request. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.
cmd_hostd_stopped: Output of `atlas hostd --stop` once the daemon accepted the shutdown.

cmd_hostd_terminal_untitled.description: Name of a running terminal that has neither a command nor a title, in the list printed by `atlas hostd --check`.
cmd_hostd_terminal_untitled.distinct: fallback name of a list row, lowercase

cmd_hostd_upgrade_failed: Warning on stderr when the hand-over of the running terminals to the new host failed; {error} is the full cause chain, already formatted. The old host keeps running.
cmd_hostd_upgrade_lost_terminals: Error of a live hand-over: the new host runs fewer terminals than the old one did; {before} and {after} are the counts. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.
cmd_hostd_upgrade_no_start: Error of a live hand-over: the new host did not answer with the new version in ten seconds. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.
cmd_hostd_upgraded_kept: Output of `atlas hostd --upgrade`: the daemon was replaced by this binary; {count} is how many running terminals moved over.
cmd_hostd_version_mismatch: Error of a restart: the host that came up reports another version than this binary. {reported} is the raw value from hostd, quotes included. Lowercase: the CLI puts `error:` before it.

cmd_hostd_version_unknown.description: The version of a terminal host that reports none, shown after "Terminal host" in `atlas hostd --check`.
cmd_hostd_version_unknown.distinct: value in a sentence about the terminal host (masculine in pt-BR)

cmd_hostd_yes_no.description: The hint after a yes/no question in the terminal: the capital letter is the default (no). Answers accepted: y, yes in English; s, sim in Portuguese; anything else is no.
cmd_hostd_yes_no.distinct: keys typed at a prompt, not words
